seed.name: microcytic anemia with liver iron overload

partners.mechanism_chain: SLC11A2 (HGNC:10954) —DISRUPTS→ Divalent Metal Transporter Activity (GO:0015374); Divalent Metal Transporter Activity (GO:0015374) —DECREASES→ Intracellular Iron (CHEBI:37977); Intracellular Iron (CHEBI:37977) —LEADS_TO→ Microcytic anemia (HP:0001945); Intracellular Iron (CHEBI:37977) —LEADS_TO→ Liver iron overload (HP:0030048); Transferrin (HGNC:11775) —DISRUPTS→ Iron transport in blood (meta:iron_transport_in_blood); Iron transport in blood (meta:iron_transport_in_blood) —DECREASES→ Serum Iron (CHEBI:17729); Serum Iron (CHEBI:17729) —LEADS_TO→ Atransferrinemia (HP:0011200); Intracellular Iron (CHEBI:37977) —LEADS_TO→ Serum Iron (CHEBI:17729). Loss of function in SLC11A2 disrupts divalent metal transporter activity, leading to reduced intracellular iron uptake and paradoxically, iron overload in the liver due to impaired cellular export and/or regulation, while also contributing to microcytic anemia. Concurrently, loss of function in Transferrin (TF) disrupts iron transport in the blood, leading to low serum iron and the phenotype of atransferrinemia. Both intracellular iron accumulation (n3) and serum iron levels (n8) are critical components of iron homeostasis, thus converging on the broader pathway of iron metabolism.

raw.translational: Understanding the interplay between heme catabolism and iron transport is crucial for developing targeted therapies for both genetic anemias and iron overload disorders.
